notes: Summary: CypressLane operates a 24/7 contact center (~1.2k agents) for a mid-size ecommerce marketplace. They're evaluating real-time agent assist to reduce AHT and escalation rates during promotional spikes.
Primary asks: streaming suggestions in-call, live ticket summarization for CRM, safe tool-calling (create/update tickets, push refunds) and deterministic guardrails to avoid policy violations.

Latency targets: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms for suggestion token responses when running with local KV cache. Throughput: baseline 200 concurrent agents, burst design for 1,500 concurrent during flash sales.
Cost sensitivity: looking to keep avg per-interaction token cost below $0.002 (target) — exploring quantized model variants + batching/caching via Redwood Optimize.
Model preferences: open quantized models preferred (13B q4 variants) with a fallback smaller model for degraded mode. Need A/B rollout testing for hallucination/regression metrics.

Security: must integrate with corporate SSO (Azure AD SAML), KMS for keys, audit logs retained 1 year, EU data residency for EU customers. Legal requested standard DPA + assurances around model data retention.
Quote from Head of Ops: 'We can't afford suggestions that hallucinate refund amounts — must be grounded to CRM state and require explicit agent confirmation.'

POC asks: 2-week Dedicated cluster in us-east + optional EU regional private control plane. Include scripted spike test (simulate 1.5k concurrent agent streams), and tool-calling demo to their Zendesk/ERP sandbox.
Internal notes: prioritize SLO validation harness, integrate our KV prefix caching on session start, verify streaming break/retry behavior and idempotency for tool calls.
Procurement path: procurement + legal have a vendor security questionnaire in drive. Forecasting suggests closing by 2026-03 if POC meets SLOs and security.
Sales tactic: offer an extended 30-day trial for Dedicated with a performance SLA for p95 latency during measured spikes to demonstrate reliability advantage over public APIs.

Potential risk: legacy telephony adapter requires a lightweight gateway; SE to confirm websocket vs. custom socket compatibility. Also need canary fallback to smaller model to maintain latency under overload.
Reference artifacts: pricing deck (drive link), security FAQ (drive link), Fireflies call IDs above. Jira ticket INF-3127 for initial infra questions.
Churn concerns: if latency or hallucination issues persist during Black Friday-like events, likely to consider in-house inference or alternate vendors with heavier SLAs.
Short-term to-do: SE (Priya) to deliver architecture diagram + costing for Dedicated pool, schedule spike run for week of 2026-02-28, legal to receive SOC2/ISO attestation by 2026-03-05.
